findings.title: Publish verification lets one upstream's candidate change or delete other upstreams' and optional sources' files and files[] lock rows (FR-012)
findings.reason: spec.md FR-012 MUST: a candidate changes only its own upstream's pins and regenerated files and MUST NOT change other upstreams or optional sources. verifyCandidate is the only trusted gate between the untrusted generate leg (which executes upstream code) and the write-token commit, and it does not enforce file ownership.
findings.x-evidence: lockDiffIssues skips the files key entirely (upstream-candidates.mjs:301) and only checks Array.isArray(files). pathPolicyIssue (L276-277) accepts any STORED_PREFIX path whose stored_at is in the base lock or candidate lock without consulting the row's upstream field. baton.lock.json files rows carry upstream atv|speckit|optimize|token-budget. Reproduced at HEAD: speckit candidate changing ATV-owned .github/agents/adversarial-reviewer.agent.md, rewriting its lock row (license Proprietary, sha256), deleting ATV-owned .github/agents/agent-native-reviewer.agent.md and changing optimize-owned packs/optimize/files/... all pass. Correctness reviewer independently raised the same gap. contracts/upstream-watch.md:61 exempts files from the exact lock comparison, so the contract is weaker than spec FR-012 (spec takes precedence).
findings.x-fix: In lockDiffIssues, key base and candidate files[] by stored_at: rows whose upstream is not the candidate id (including optional sources) must be byte-identical, not added or removed, and no row may change its upstream. In pathPolicyIssue, accept a changed/deleted STORED_PREFIX path only when the owning lock row (base for deleted/changed-existing, candidate for new) has upstream === id. Amend contracts/upstream-watch.md FR-012 rule accordingly. Add unit and integration tamper cases for both directions (speckit->atv/optional, atv->speckit/optional) with exact E_PATH_POLICY/E_CANDIDATE_VERIFY codes and no writes.
findings.x-review2: Fixed at 6d505f9 for every row present in the base lock: lockDiffIssues keys files[] by stored_at and freezes other upstreams/optional sources, forbids owner changes and foreign additions; pathPolicyIssue checks base-row owner. Unit + 13 integration tamper cases with no writes. The residual unlocked-tracked-path gap is tracked separately as F14.

findings.title: Publish rewrites a candidate PR closed during the run, and the next run then suppresses a pin no human rejected
findings.reason: FR-021 suppresses only the exact pin a human closed. Publish pushes under a lease and PATCHes item.pr without re-reading PR state; unlike closeObsolete (L424) there is no state/head re-check. If a maintainer closes the PR mid-run with the branch untouched, the lease still holds, the closed PR body gets the new marker pin, and planUpstream (upstream-candidates.mjs:207) suppresses the new pin next run.
findings.x-fix: Before push and PATCH of an existing PR, re-fetch it and require state open and head.sha equal to item.branch.sha; otherwise record a non-writing outcome/blocker. Add an integration case closing the PR between detect and publish.
findings.x-review2: Fixed: publish re-reads the PR (open, head == detected branch sha) before push and fails E_PR_CHANGED with no writes (upstream-upgrade.mjs:490-494); tests at upstream-upgrade.test.mjs 680/738. Null-PR race tracked as F21.

findings.title: Candidate artifacts are bound only by name across matrix legs that run untrusted code
findings.reason: Publish/report download pattern candidate-* and select by name; all generate legs share the run's Actions runtime token, so a compromised upstream leg could upload or pre-empt the other leg's candidate-<id> artifact. verifyCandidate binds only to public plan values. Impact after F01 is fixed is limited to allowlisted content attributed to the other upstream's PR, still reviewed as a draft; defense-in-depth.
findings.x-fix: Expose upload-artifact artifact-id/digest as per-leg outputs (or per-upstream jobs) and have publish/report download by artifact-ids and verify the digest; document in contracts/upstream-watch.md.
findings.x-review2: Fixed: per-leg <id>_artifact/<id>_digest outputs gated on matrix.upstream, downloads by artifact-ids into artifacts/<id>, publish compares DIGEST_<ID> to verified digest. verifyCandidate remains the real trust gate (digest is attested by the leg that ran upstream code). ATV-leg test gap tracked as F16; live matrix-output behavior pending post-merge.

findings.title: sync --bump failure (E_DANGLING_REF path) never asserted end-to-end through report
findings.reason: The known R-SPECKIT-CLOSURE failure is the expected first live Spec Kit outcome. Code path verified by reading: BUMP_OUTCOME failure -> package blocker E_UPSTREAM_VERIFY (generate) with bump.log tail -> renderIssue row + Blockers fenced excerpt, issue stays open, report fails the run; this satisfies FR-024 and SC-001's 'names the blocker'. But the only bump-failure test stops at package/publish; report rendering and exit for that blocker are covered only via the shared E_CHECK_FAILED path.
findings.x-fix: Add a report test with BUMP_LOG containing an E_DANGLING_REF line asserting exit 1, row E_UPSTREAM_VERIFY (generate), Blockers entry and fenced excerpt containing E_DANGLING_REF.
findings.x-review2: Fixed (simulated): E_DANGLING_REF log through package/publish/report asserts E_UPSTREAM_VERIFY (generate) row, fenced excerpt and no PR. Real Spec Kit bump remains the accepted upstream limitation.

findings.title: Any '[remote rejected]' push (protected branch, hook) is misreported as E_LEASE 'changed since detection'
findings.reason: Regex /stale info|rejected|fetch first|non-fast-forward/ matches git porcelain '[remote rejected]'; a permanent configuration failure is reported as a transient race.
findings.x-fix: Map only stale-info/fetch-first/non-fast-forward [rejected] to E_LEASE; map [remote rejected] to E_PUSH with the reason. Add a test.
findings.x-review2: Fixed: [remote rejected] maps to E_PUSH with reason, [rejected]/stale to E_LEASE; pre-receive hook test. Generic fallback untested (F17).

findings.title: Artifact-controlled paths are interpolated into inline code in the bot PR body and can break out into live Markdown
findings.reason: pathPolicyIssue rejects only control chars, backslash and non-normalized segments; a backtick-containing stored_at listed in the candidate lock closes the code span and allows mentions/links in a github-actions[bot] draft PR body.
findings.x-fix: Restrict paths to a conservative character set in pathPolicyIssue, or render file lists inside a fenced block via sanitizeExcerpt. Add a test.
findings.x-review2: Fixed: SAFE_PATH [A-Za-z0-9._/@+-] enforced in pathPolicyIssue; all 133 current lock rows comply; backtick and space tests.

findings.title: Ownership and suppression depend on an editable PR-body marker
findings.reason: Removing the marker from an open bot-only PR body makes it waiting-human forever (never refreshed or closed obsolete); removing it from a closed unmerged PR body lifts FR-021 suppression and a new PR for the rejected pin is opened. Both are fail-safe or human-caused but are reported misleadingly. Merged from two adversarial findings (originally P2 and P3); downgraded because no data loss or write to human work occurs.
findings.x-fix: Report a specific marker blocker instead of waiting-human for bot-only branches with a missing marker, and fall back to the closed bot PR title/branch head trailer (Baton-Pin) for suppression.
findings.x-review2: Fixed in code: open bot-only marker-less PR blocks E_PR_MARKER; closed marker-less PR suppresses via titlePin. Spec traceability/human decision tracked as F15; title duplication as F18.

findings.title: Manifest checks comparison is a constant echo, not a validation gate
findings.reason: packageCandidate always writes CHECKS after the BUMP/CHECK outcome early returns; an untrusted artifact can copy the constant. The authoritative gate is the generate step outcomes plus result.json blocker absence, which publish trusts from the same untrusted leg. Message 'required checks did not pass' overstates what is verified; the PR body validation claim is therefore attested by the read-only leg only (draft + ready_for_review CI is the backstop).
findings.x-fix: Rename the rejection to a schema check and document the trust boundary in contracts/upstream-watch.md and the PR body checklist.
findings.x-review2: Fixed in source: schema-mismatch wording, contentDigest excludes checks, PR body and contract state the trust boundary. Missing assertion of the new message tracked as F17.

findings.title: Test gaps on trust/lifecycle edges: manifest.pin tamper, exact lock-diff issue assertions, truncated compare list, collectResults fallbacks
findings.reason: Tamper lists never mutate manifest.pin; lock-diff mutation cases assert only non-empty issues; no case where compare total_commits exceeds listed commits (fail-closed human protection at upstream-upgrade.mjs:184); no report test for missing artifact (E_CHECK_FAILED), incomplete publish (E_PUBLISH) or malformed PLAN (failedPlan). Merged from four testing findings.
findings.x-fix: Add the four case groups with exact codes/messages and no-write assertions.
findings.x-review2: Fixed: manifest pin tamper (unit+integration), exact lock-diff messages, truncated compare -> waiting-human with no writes, report fallbacks.

findings.title: Docs name the tracking issue 'upstream-watch' but the code uses title 'Upstream watch: releases and verification' and label upstream-bump; local stage invocation/env is undocumented
findings.reason: Agents and maintainers following the docs cannot find the issue by name or reproduce detect/package/report locally without reading the workflow; detect/report outputs are silent without GITHUB_OUTPUT/GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. Merged from three agent-native findings; local preview downgraded from P2 because FR-027 requires only hosted dispatch preview.
findings.x-fix: Name the exact issue title and label (gh issue list --label upstream-bump), and add a short maintainer note on stage env inputs or print plan/summary to stdout when the Actions files are unset.
findings.x-review2: Fixed: docs name title "Upstream watch: releases and verification", label upstream-bump and stage invocation. Residual wording inaccuracies tracked as F19.

findings.title: Carried ATV note can contradict a release-tracking pin; repo slugs and SHA/semver validators duplicated
findings.reason: The note is maintainer-owned by contract (contracts/upstream-watch.md:65), so preserving it is intended, but after sync --bump atv=<x.y.z> the 'pinned to main' note stays stale and automation cannot change it; docs do not say to edit it. Separately, owner/repo literals (upstream-upgrade.mjs:37-38, sync.mjs:322,328,354,358) and inline /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/ copies (upstream-upgrade.mjs:131,181,250) duplicate exported constants/helpers on the trust boundary. Merged maintainability findings; P2 note finding downgraded because it is contract-intended.
findings.x-fix: Document in docs/07-updating.md that switching ATV policy requires a maintainer note edit; derive API paths/lock repo/links from one slug and reuse isSha/isVersion.
findings.x-review2: Fixed in substance: ATV note preserved and documented as maintainer-owned; repo fields from SPECKIT_REPO/ATV_REPO; isSha reused in upstream-upgrade. Residual duplication tracked as F20.

findings.title: Removing the label or retitling the tracking issue creates a duplicate issue
findings.reason: Pre-existing behavior: the base workflow at ae34a99 already located the issue by labels=upstream-bump plus exact title. Not introduced by this feature and not required by FR-023.

findings.title: FR-012 ownership still bypassable: a candidate can claim and overwrite tracked-but-unlocked stored paths by adding its own files[] row
findings.reason: spec.md FR-012 MUST and contracts/upstream-watch.md:51-54 allow the candidate-lock row as owner only for a NEW path. pathPolicyIssue falls back to the untrusted candidate-lock row for any changed path absent from the base lock, and fileRowIssues accepts added rows for the candidate own upstream, so existing tracked files that no lock row owns can be overwritten by a candidate whose generate leg ran upstream code.
findings.x-evidence: upstream-candidates.mjs:301 owner = base row ?? (kind changed ? candidate row). 13 tracked unlocked paths under STORED_PREFIX at 6d505f9 include .specify/memory/constitution.md, .github/skills/baton/SKILL.md, .github/skills/baton-review/SKILL.md, .github/skills/baton-land/SKILL.md, packs/learning/files/.atv/.gitignore and optimize/token-budget pack files. Orchestrator probe: speckit candidate adding {stored_at: .specify/memory/constitution.md, upstream: speckit} and changing it -> pathPolicyIssue null, lockDiffIssues []. Learnings (per-checkout-identity-self-review) and testing reviewers concur; no test covers it. Pre-existing at ad5f4a6, missed by review 1.
findings.x-fix: In verifyCandidate/publish, accept the candidate-lock row as owner only when the path does not exist in the base tree (pass the base tree path set from git ls-tree -r --name-only <base>, or check git cat-file -e <base>:<path>); otherwise require a base-lock row owned by the candidate. Add unit and integration tamper cases (tracked unlocked path change -> E_PATH_POLICY, no writes) and a genuinely new path acceptance case.

findings.title: D5/D-REVIEW1-GATE describe the amendment as pure FR-010/012/024 tightening, but marker-less blocking (E_PR_MARKER precedence) and title-based suppression are new FR-019/FR-021 lifecycle choices without a recorded human decision
findings.reason: Constitution IV and the BATON preamble require a recorded human decision when a public contract changes. No gate was bypassed and no approval is claimed (review->implement is ungated; land gate remains), but the trace is inaccurate and the marker-less rules need explicit human acceptance.
findings.x-evidence: handoff.md:299-309 D5/D-REVIEW1-GATE; contracts/upstream-watch.md Missing markers section; upstream-candidates.mjs:205 E_PR_MARKER evaluated before obsolete/none so an unmarked bot PR blocks every run even when nothing is newer; :213 titlePin fallback is defeated if the PR is retitled before closing (adversarial). Neither rule is in spec FR-019/FR-021.
findings.x-fix: Correct D5, D-REVIEW1-GATE and the Phase 8 intro to cite FR-019/020/021/022 for F02/F07 changes, record that marker-less blocking and title suppression are new behavior, and either obtain a recorded human decision at the land gate or route a needs-human question. Consider evaluating none/obsolete before E_PR_MARKER and document E_PR_MARKER recovery (closing also suppresses).

findings.title: ATV artifact/digest leg is not exercised end to end and the per-upstream workflow blocks are hand-repeated without a structural test
findings.reason: F03 correctness for atv rests only on YAML string assertions (maintainer-workflows.test.mjs:241); a wiring drift in publish or report download for one upstream silently degrades to no candidate.
findings.x-evidence: DIGEST_ATV/artifacts/atv absent from integration tests; workflow repeats outputs (96-99), downloads in publish (169-180) and report (209-220), env 189-190. Maintainability and testing reviewers concur.
findings.x-fix: Loop the missing/mismatched digest cases over speckit and atv with an atv happy-path publish; add a workflow test asserting, for each UPSTREAMS id, gated outputs, a download step in publish and report with path artifacts/<id>, and DIGEST_<ID>.

findings.title: titlePin duplicates the prTitle format and hardcodes (speckit|atv) without a round-trip test
findings.reason: Suppression of marker-less closed PRs depends on titlePin parsing exactly what prTitle (line 440) emits; a wording change silently disables suppression and reopens declined bumps.
findings.x-fix: Share one title prefix helper between prTitle and titlePin and add a round-trip test for speckit version, atv version and atv SHA.

findings.title: Operator docs: stage paragraph overstates "reads only environment variables" and the shared variable set; new blocker codes have no remedies; missing vs mismatched digest share one excerpt
findings.reason: detect/package read the checkout and lock and publish/report read ARTIFACTS_DIR; GITHUB_REF/PREVIEW are read by detect (and report), package needs PLAN. E_PR_MARKER/E_PR_CHANGED/E_PUSH/E_LEASE/E_CANDIDATE_VERIFY remedies are only in the spec contract, unlike docs/04-handoffs.md code table. upstream-upgrade.mjs:480-482 uses one message for an empty DIGEST_<ID> (wiring) and a mismatch (tamper).
findings.x-fix: Reword the stage paragraph per actual inputs, add a blocker-code remedy table, and distinguish an empty attested digest in the E_CANDIDATE_VERIFY excerpt with a test.

findings.title: F11 consolidation incomplete: parseBump keeps inline SHA/semver regex and the repo slug is derived in two places
findings.reason: The CLI bump parser and the workflow pin validators (isSha/isVersion) can drift on the pin trust boundary; sync.mjs:12 slug() and upstream-upgrade.mjs:36-37 inline URL pathname duplicate the same derivation.
findings.x-fix: Export a repo slug helper and the pin predicates from one module and use them in parseBump and upstream-upgrade.

findings.title: PR opened on the bot branch after detect (item.pr null) is not re-checked: publish pushes into it, POST fails 422 and later runs block with E_PR_MARKER
findings.reason: The F02 re-read runs only when item.pr is set; the lease still matches because the branch did not move. Narrow window requiring a maintainer to open a PR from the bot branch mid-run; recoverable by closing the PR, hence P3 (adversarial rated P2).
findings.x-fix: When item.pr is null, list open PRs for head owner:branch immediately before push and fail E_PR_CHANGED if one exists; test it.
